claim: Boden's three types are usable as executable operators for an LLM (analogy transfer, systematic search inside a space, rule change), but the mode-specific part adds only modest value over a plain search wrapper: full operator preferred in 58.3% (combinational), 54.2% (transformational), about 52% (exploratory) of paired comparisons against ablated versions (chance 50%).
agent_test: At equal tokens, run C/E/T operator prompts versus a plain best-first search wrapper on our open-mode tasks, judged by a position-debiased pairwise judge.

claim: Which Boden mode wins depends on the task and the backbone. Transformational mode scored best on low-constraint tasks (Bridge 0.680, Electricity 0.620 human creativity vs OnePrompt 0.480, 0.540 with GPT-4o), exploratory mode won on 100 hypothesis tasks with Qwen3-14B (win rate 32.7% vs 25.5% next best), and on GLM-4-9B plain OnePrompt ranked first (46.3%).
agent_test: Route by constraint level: test exploratory generator for well-specified tasks, rule-dropping for low-constraint tasks, and a plain prompt as the control arm, on at least two backbones.

claim: Mode-specific search costs many more tokens and quality does not rise with tokens: relative to one prompt, ToT 7.4x, E-UoT 10.0x, EGoT 27.6x, C-UoT 36.5x, T-UoT 52.5x, yet the cheapest structured method (E-UoT) was best.
agent_test: Report every generator arm at matched token budget; drop any arm that loses to E-UoT-style search at 10x.

claim: Current LLM analogy transfer fails at the transfer step, not at retrieval: C-UoT picked a valid analogue 100% of the time but strong transfer was 52% on tasks it won versus 32% on tasks it lost.
agent_test: Add a check step after analogy retrieval that tests whether the mapped mechanism is specific and carries over; measure strong-transfer rate.

claim: Scaling and search help combination more than exploration: CreativeBench Qwen2.5-7B Combo creativity 0.168 vs Explore 0.0146; Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite Combo 0.509 vs Explore 0.1681; evolutionary search and EvoRePE steering lift both only slightly (Combo 0.168 to 0.193; Explore 0.0146 to 0.0182).
agent_test: Measure our agent on a combinational and an exploratory subset separately; expect exploration to be the weak side.

claim: On reasoning tasks, RL on one skill generalizes within the same skill (exploratory) but not to composed or transformed skills: Zebra Logic base 30%, +61 points in-distribution, +53 out-of-distribution; Geometry +31 vs +8; matrix-rank transformative OOD fell from 70% by 30 points after RL.
schema_part: S3 (boundary: scaffold cannot replace new rules)
agent_test: Test whether scaffolded search at inference time recovers the transformative OOD cases where RL regressed.

claim: More samples do not cure failure at high complexity: pass@k rises toward 100% at low complexity but is 0 at level 6 even at 64 attempts, though a DP solver needs only 36 states; the model spends a smaller share of tokens on computation and more on conjecture.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare best-of-N against a staged search that forces computation steps on hard instances.

claim: LLM research ideas can be rated more novel than expert human ideas but are less diverse: novelty 5.64 vs 4.84 (p<0.01), AI+human rerank 5.81; feasibility slightly lower; of 4000 seeds per topic only 200 were non-duplicate.
agent_test: Add a duplicate filter (embedding similarity) to the generator and track non-duplicate yield per token.

claim: Aligned LLMs produce homogeneous output: lower diversity after RLHF/DPO (Mohammadi 2024; Kirk et al. cited), 1.1M poems collapse onto few rhymes (top 1% of rhyme pairs cover 30.7-49.8% of occurrences), and the Artificial Hivemind study reports cosine similarity above 0.8 in 79% of pools. The size of the effect is disputed (see next claim).
agent_test: Measure our agent's output diversity across 20 reruns with and without a diversity prompt.

claim: The strength of the homogeneity claim is overstated by its null: different-idea pairs already exceed cosine 0.8 in 20% (LLM labels) to 32% (clusters) of cases, so the original same-prompt pairs exceed it only 1.9-3.1 times as often.
agent_test: Never use raw cosine threshold alone; label ideas by distinct concept and compare with a different-idea null.

claim: Cheap diversity interventions work without training: verbalized sampling gives 1.6-2.1x creative-writing diversity; random-prefix decoding gives LLM-rated diversity 0.68 vs 0.33 with relevance 0.98 vs 0.99; weight steering gives originality d=+0.36 (utility drops).
agent_test: Prompt-only: test verbalized sampling inside the generator at equal tokens. Random-prefix and steering need decoding or weight access, so not available to a scaffold.

claim: Diversity gains are bounded by the true answer space: for topics with a finite answer set the random-prefix method saturates, and for idea generation the non-duplicate pool plateaus. Gap search: independent batches without memory plateau near batch 60 (cluster count flat), and a persistent duplicate memory cut collapse from 5.6% to 0.0% (Lingo and Chhajer 2026, 2-3 seeds).
agent_test: Stop generation when new non-duplicate yield falls below a threshold; test token saving.

claim: LLM agents explore regions humans did not but this does not raise performance: AIDE GPT-5 H-creativity 1.423 vs gold-medal human 0.744, yet medal rate only 21.25%; creativity falls and performance rises over iterations for both humans and agents; greedy, MCTS and evolutionary search policies converged.
agent_test: Track novelty per iteration; test a schedule that explores early and refines late versus constant mix.

claim: Judging creativity is the weak link: LLM raters agree poorly with experts on creative writing (no LLM-administered test correlated positively with expert annotation; LLM stories pass 3-10x fewer tests than expert-rated New Yorker stories at 84.7%), while a tuned GPT-5 judge reaches Spearman 0.732 with human P-creativity labels, and KOMBINE LLM panels agree with humans 66% (majority) to 75% (unanimous). Gap search: one style-flip probe (50 cells) moved an LLM creativity judge by only +0.40 and +0.52 points on a 10-50 scale, but the same judge agrees more with LLM gold (0.80) than human gold (0.65, n=718).
agent_test: Calibrate our judge against 30 human-labelled items per task; use only unanimous multi-judge panels.

claim: Automated novelty metrics may favour stylistic over conceptual novelty and shift under prompt changes. Gap search opened AGC-Bench: a register-only paraphrase barely moved its judge (d=0.15 to 0.29), so stylistic bias is small there, but the probe did not test conceptual reordering. The Lu et al. 2026 execution-audit claim was still not located.
agent_test: Check our novelty judge under prompt paraphrase; require stable rank.

claim: Transformational creativity (changing the rules of the space) is argued unreachable by training alone, but no experiment shows this, and scaffolds that simulate rule change (UoT T-UoT, Denial Prompting) report gains on low-constraint or checkable tasks. Gap search: Denial Prompting correctness falls with each added rule (GPT-4 pass@1 16.1% to 2.1% over five rules) while divergence rises; formal work says real transformation edits axioms with many dependents, which a technique ban does not.
agent_test: Test a rule-drop operator (name the constraints, drop one, regenerate) against sampling at equal tokens on checkable tasks.

claim: Denial Prompting (forbid the previous technique step by step) exposes limits: GPT-4 was best at nearly every step, Claude-3 and Llama3-70B fell to 0 within two steps, and only MCTS among four reasoning strategies raised divergent creativity (gain 0 after step 2).
agent_test: Use Denial-style forbidden-technique steps as a cheap check on whether open mode actually changes approach.

claim: LLMs beat humans at some combinational tasks but converge: KOMBINE finds LLMs 10-16 points better at association and analogy than 75 humans, yet 19.9% (412/2,070) of invented concepts reuse a property another model invented, and a blending explanation step helps text-to-image mashups (rank 1.98 vs 2.40).
agent_test: Add an explicit explanation-of-shared-attributes step before blending and measure novelty plus cross-run overlap.

claim: Search with an LLM as mutation operator plus an evaluator produces new valid artefacts (Sodarace 1,728 niches; AlphaEvolve matched or beat best known on 52 of 54 tensor targets, 14 surpassed), supporting exploratory creativity as search with automatic checks.
agent_test: Use only where we have an automatic verifier; otherwise this arm is unavailable.

claim: Wiggins formalisation gives exploration as search in a rule-defined space (R, T, E) and transformation as search over spaces; later formal work (Espirito Santo et al. 2024; Schapiro et al. 2025) rebuilds this but no measurement has validated the formal definitions on LLM agents.
agent_test: Operationalise R, T, E in the prompt (list constraints, traversal rule, evaluation) and test if explicit lists beat unlabeled generation.

claim: In Denial Prompting on 199 Codeforces problems, each added forbidden technique cuts correctness and constraint following while raising divergent novelty: GPT-4 pass@1 16.1, 11.6, 7.1, 5.2, 2.3, 2.1 percent over states 0 to 5, constraint following 100 to 14.4 percent, divergent creativity 4.5 to 15.3 percent. Claude-3 and Llama3-70B reach zero joint score within two states.
agent_test: On a checkable task, run rule-drop for 1, 2, 3 rules and plot pass rate; cap the number of drops where pass rate halves.

claim: The cheapest known validity check for a changed rule is two-part: the original correctness test still passes, and a separate detector confirms the forbidden element is absent (GPT-4 technique detector, 94% recall in a pilot). Prose tasks have no equivalent test; licensed versus unlicensed invention (Whiteboard: humans license 18.7-22.8% of unsupported content) needs a goal check.
agent_test: After each rule change, require a test or a second-call check against the original goal; log failures per rule.

claim: Formal accounts say transformation edits the rule set or axioms of a conceptual space, and the most transformative edits hit axioms with many dependents (Schapiro et al. 2025 Theorem 4; Wiggins 2019 as quoted). A prompt that bans one technique edits a leaf rule, so it likely meets only a weak form of transformation. The primary Boden and Wiggins texts were not opened.
agent_test: Test an axiom-level operator (list assumptions, drop one that many others depend on, re-derive) against a leaf-rule ban on checkable tasks.

claim: No independent replication of Universe of Thoughts was found in arXiv title and abstract searches or in Semantic Scholar citations (zero citing items). All Boden-typed LLM mode results remain single-paper. A negative search result, limited by rate limits.
agent_test: Replicate on a second backbone and a judge from another family before building mode routing on UoT.

claim: Creativity-promoting wrappers do not reliably raise quality in the novel region: over 4 models, q@Tail versus vanilla 0.474 was +17.7% for min-p sampling and negative for convergent-divergent thinking (-6.9%), persona (-11.2%), branch-solve-merge (-13.9%), self-consistency (-19.0%) and meta-prompting (-32.5%).
agent_test: Score the open mode on quality within the most novel quarter of outputs, not on novelty alone.

claim: A single general creativity factor explains 81.5% of variance across 83 LLMs on 78 datasets, correlated with reasoning (rho 0.55) yet separable. Backbone strength therefore likely dominates mode choice, which fits the backbone flips seen in Universe of Thoughts.
agent_test: Fix the backbone first; compare modes only within one backbone and report the rank on a second.

claim: Set-level prompting (3 ideas in one response) raises idea distance from 0.24 to about 0.80 versus independent samples but lowers win rate (Claude Opus 4.8: 0.33 to 0.21); training with a set-level reward reached CU 0.64 vs 0.38 for Opus. No scaffold-only method is shown to get both gains.
agent_test: Use set prompting in the explore step, then a quality filter; measure win rate and distance together.

claim: The explore-then-refine split (40% broad exploration, 60% gap filling) is used in Dynamic Context Evolution but never compared with a constant mix; the self-rated obviousness filter is weak (Spearman -0.065 against distance from centroid) and overlaps only 3% with duplicate rejection. Gap 8 (schedule benefit, human pattern) stays open.
agent_test: Run a schedule ablation: constant mix versus explore-then-refine at equal tokens on one checkable task.

claim: Cheap diversity measure without a judge: semantic entropy over clustered meanings agrees with human preference at rho 0.56 (above cosine, Self-BLEU, Distinct-n) and tracks an LLM novelty judge validated at rho 0.80 on 30 pairs; divergent score did not rise with model size while convergent did. Small human panels.
agent_test: Use clustered-meaning entropy as the open-mode stop signal; validate once against a human sample.
